answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks by depositing stake across graph clusters. In the falcon protocol, an auditor scans transaction graphs for sparse topological cuts. If clustered fake identities attempt to isolate traffic like an artificial nebula in an open meadow, multi-agent auditing exposes the cut, triggering stake slashing. Because verifying cuts across expanding clusters requires cross-bonding, attacker cost scales superlinearly with node count.
